title: Horizontal deleted-vertex reindexing of shuffle words with signs
statement:
For any set $S$, let $\mathbf Z[S]$ be the free $\mathbf Z$-module with basis $S$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]; evaluated strings below can equivalently be read as basis symbols in the free module on strings of their length. Let $a,b\geq0$, $n=a+b$, and let $W_{a,b}$ be the finite set of words $w_0\cdots w_{n-1}$ with $a$ letters $H$ and $b$ letters $V$. Put $A_k(w)=\#\{r<k:w_r=H\}$ and $B_k(w)=\#\{r<k:w_r=V\}$ for $0\leq k\leq n$. Let $I(w)=\#\{(r,s):r<s,\ w_r=V,\ w_s=H\}$ and $s(w)=(-1)^{I(w)}\in\mathbf Z$. For any sets $X,Y$ and sequences $u=(u_0,\ldots,u_a)$ in $X$, $v=(v_0,\ldots,v_b)$ in $Y$, write $z_{u,v}(w)=((u_{A_k(w)},v_{B_k(w)}))_{k=0}^n$ and let $d_k$ denote deletion of entry $k$ of a sequence. No distinctness of sequence entries is assumed.

Assume $a>0$. Let $H_{a,b}$ consist of the labeled pairs $(w,k)$ with $w\in W_{a,b}$ and either $k=0,w_0=H$, or $k=n,w_{n-1}=H$, or $0<k<n,w_{k-1}=w_k=H$. There is a bijection
$$\Phi_H:H_{a,b}\xrightarrow{\sim}\{0,\ldots,a\}\times W_{a-1,b}.$$
At an interior pair it is $(w,k)\mapsto(i,\bar w)$, where $i=A_k(w)$ and $\bar w$ replaces the two neighboring $H$ letters by one; here $1\leq i<a$. At $k=0$ it removes the initial $H$ and sets $i=0$; at $k=n$ it removes the terminal $H$ and sets $i=a$. Its inverse for $0<i<a$ splits the $i$-th $H$ of $\bar w$ (counted from one) into two $H$ letters and marks the intervening vertex; for $i=0,a$ it prepends or appends $H$ and marks that endpoint, respectively. If $\Phi_H(w,k)=(i,\bar w)$, then
$$d_kz_{u,v}(w)=z_{d_i u,v}(\bar w),\qquad s(w)(-1)^k=(-1)^i s(\bar w).$$
More precisely, at an interior pair, $t=B_k(w)$ satisfies $k=i+t$ and $I(w)=I(\bar w)+t$; at the initial endpoint $I(w)=I(\bar w)$; at the terminal endpoint $I(w)=I(\bar w)+b$ and $k=a+b$. These assertions include $a=1$ (only endpoint faces) and $b=0$. If $a=0$, the same labeled horizontal set is empty.

proof.text: Define $\Phi_H$ by the stated removals. Each removes exactly one $H$ and no $V$, so $\bar w\in W_{a-1,b}$. At an interior mark, the $H$ at position $k-1$ is counted by $A_k$ and the $H$ at position $k$ is not; thus $1\leq i=A_k(w)\leq a-1$. Endpoints have labels $0$ and $a$. Hence the map has the required codomain.

proof.text: For $0<i<a$, write $\bar w=P H Q$ at its $i$-th $H$ (counted from one). Set $w=P H H Q$ and $k=|P|+1$. Then $0<k<n$, the neighboring letters are $H,H$, and $A_k(w)=i$ since $P$ has $i-1$ horizontal letters. Collapsing this pair returns $\bar w$. Conversely, an interior pair has exactly $i-1$ horizontal letters before its first marked $H$, so splitting that $i$-th $H$ recovers both its word and its mark. Prepending/appending $H$ and marking $0/n$ are likewise inverse to the endpoint removals. The three label ranges $\{0\}$, $\{1,\ldots,a-1\}$, $\{a\}$ are disjoint because $a>0$; these inverse identities prove bijectivity on labeled pairs.

source.place: Paragraph (3), universal shuffle input below the open direct-image argument; agent-written horizontal-face calculation (the blueprint states the application only).

proof.text: At an interior pair, for shorter-word vertex indices $0\leq r<n$, direct prefix counting gives $(A_r(\bar w),B_r(\bar w))=(A_r(w),B_r(w))$ if $r<k$, and $(A_{r+1}(w)-1,B_{r+1}(w))$ if $r\geq k$. In the first range $A_r(w)<i$; in the second $A_{r+1}(w)>i$, since the two marked horizontal steps straddle vertex $k$. The sequence $d_i u$ takes index $h$ to $u_h$ for $h<i$ and to $u_{h+1}$ for $h\geq i$. Substituting the two prefix formulas shows that its evaluated vertex $r$ is the original vertex $r$ for $r<k$ and $r+1$ for $r\geq k$, with the same vertical coordinate. This is exactly $d_k z_{u,v}(w)=z_{d_i u,v}(\bar w)$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), universal shuffle input below the open direct-image argument; agent-written horizontal-face calculation (the blueprint states the application only).

proof.text: At $k=0$, deleting the initial $H$ gives $(A_r(\bar w),B_r(\bar w))=(A_{r+1}(w)-1,B_{r+1}(w))$ for $0\leq r<n$. Since $(d_0u)_h=u_{h+1}$, these are precisely the original vertices $1,\ldots,n$. At $k=n$, removal of the terminal $H$ leaves $(A_r,B_r)$ unchanged for $0\leq r<n$, and $A_r(w)\leq a-1$ there, so $(d_a u)_{A_r(w)}=u_{A_r(w)}$. These are precisely vertices $0,\ldots,n-1$. Thus the evaluated-sequence identity also holds at both endpoints.

source.place: Paragraph (3), universal shuffle input below the open direct-image argument; agent-written horizontal-face calculation (the blueprint states the application only).

proof.text: For an interior collapse, regard the removed letter as the second of the two adjacent $H$ letters, at position $k$. The retained letters have the same relative order, so their inversion pairs correspond bijectively to those of $\bar w$. The inversion pairs lost are exactly those whose second letter is this removed $H$ and whose first letter is an earlier $V$; there are $t=B_k(w)$ of them. Therefore $I(w)=I(\bar w)+t$. Partitioning the first $k$ letters into horizontal and vertical letters gives $k=A_k(w)+B_k(w)=i+t$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), universal shuffle input below the open direct-image argument; agent-written horizontal-face calculation (the blueprint states the application only).

proof.text: Removing an initial $H$ loses no inversion: no $V$ precedes it, and an $H$ cannot be the first letter of a $V,H$ inversion. Removing a terminal $H$ loses exactly $b$ inversions, one for each $V$. All retained inversion pairs preserve their order as before. Thus $I(w)=I(\bar w)$ initially and $I(w)=I(\bar w)+b$ terminally, where $k=n=a+b$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), universal shuffle input below the open direct-image argument; agent-written horizontal-face calculation (the blueprint states the application only).

proof.text: In the interior the preceding formulas yield $s(w)(-1)^k=(-1)^{I(\bar w)+t+i+t}=(-1)^i s(\bar w)$ because $(-1)^{2t}=1$. Initially $k=i=0$ and the inversion counts agree. Terminally $i=a$ and $I(w)+k=I(\bar w)+b+a+b=I(\bar w)+a+2b$, giving the same sign formula. These are identities of integer powers.

source.place: Paragraph (3), universal shuffle input below the open direct-image argument; agent-written horizontal-face calculation (the blueprint states the application only).

proof.text: When $a=1$ no interior pair is possible, since it would require two horizontal letters; the inverse construction has only the two endpoint labels and works even when $b=0$. When $b=0$ all vertical prefix counts and inversion counts are zero, and the same formulas still apply (the unique shorter word may be empty). When $a=0$ there is no horizontal letter, so none of the horizontal marking conditions can hold; for the empty word there is no endpoint letter either. All sequence equalities above compare indices before evaluating $u$ and $v$, so repeated entries cause no identification of labeled pairs. Equal strings also determine equal basis symbols in the free module of [def-weil-pbc-free-module]; its statement gives uniqueness of finite basis expansions, without imposing distinctness on the entries within a basis string.

lean.statement: theorem horizontal_face_reindexing (a b : ℕ) : IsEmpty (HorizontalFace 0 b) ∧ ∃ Φ : HorizontalFace (a + 1) b ≃ Fin (a + 2) × Word a b, (∀ p : HorizontalFace (a + 1) b, (Φ p).1.val = horizontalCount p.val.1 p.val.2 ∧ (Φ p).2.val = p.val.1.val.eraseIdx (min p.val.2 (a + 1 + b - 1)) ∧ (0 < p.val.2 ∧ p.val.2 < a + 1 + b → 1 ≤ (Φ p).1.val ∧ (Φ p).1.val < a + 1 ∧ p.val.2 = (Φ p).1.val + verticalCount p.val.1 p.val.2 ∧ inversions p.val.1 = inversions (Φ p).2 + verticalCount p.val.1 p.val.2) ∧ (p.val.2 = 0 → (Φ p).1.val = 0 ∧ inversions p.val.1 = inversions (Φ p).2) ∧ (p.val.2 = a + 1 + b → (Φ p).1.val = a + 1 ∧ inversions p.val.1 = inversions (Φ p).2 + b) ∧ sign p.val.1 * (-1 : ℤ) ^ p.val.2 = (-1 : ℤ) ^ (Φ p).1.val * sign (Φ p).2) ∧ (∀ q : Fin (a + 2) × Word a b, (q.1.val = 0 → (Φ.symm q).val.1.val = false :: q.2.val ∧ (Φ.symm q).val.2 = 0) ∧ (q.1.val = a + 1 → (Φ.symm q).val.1.val = q.2.val ++ [false] ∧ (Φ.symm q).val.2 = a + 1 + b) ∧ (0 < q.1.val ∧ q.1.val < a + 1 → ∃ P Q : List Bool, q.2.val = P ++ false :: Q ∧ P.count false + 1 = q.1.val ∧ (Φ.symm q).val.1.val = P ++ false :: false :: Q ∧ (Φ.symm q).val.2 = P.length + 1)) ∧ (∀ (X : Type u) (Y : Type v) (x : Fin (a + 1 + 1) → X) (y : Fin (b + 1) → Y) (p : HorizontalFace (a + 1) b), (evaluate p.val.1 x y).eraseIdx p.val.2 = evaluate (Φ p).2 (Fin.removeNth (Φ p).1 x) y ∧ Finsupp.single ((evaluate p.val.1 x y).eraseIdx p.val.2) (1 : ℤ) = Finsupp.single (evaluate (Φ p).2 (Fin.removeNth (Φ p).1 x) y) (1 : ℤ))
